title: Reddit keeps its strange DMCA fight over Google search results alive
gist: US District Judge Paul A. Engelmayer largely denied SerpApi's motion to dismiss Reddit's DMCA anti-circumvention suit alleging SerpApi built a tool to bypass Google's access controls and Perplexity AI paid for it — surviving where a parallel Google claim was dismissed two weeks earlier, because Reddit pleaded a specific licensing term requiring partners to delete flagged posts. If Reddit prevails, it gains a lever to force all AI scrapers into licensing agreements, though a DMCA expert notes Reddit is not the copyright owner, exclusive licensee, or deployer of the protection measure.

insights.claim: US District Judge Paul A. Engelmayer largely denied web scraper SerpApi's motion to dismiss, finding Reddit plausibly pleaded a conspiracy in which SerpApi supplied a product to circumvent Google access controls and Perplexity AI paid for it.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: A surviving DMCA anti-circumvention theory against a scraping-plus-AI-buyer pair opens a litigation channel that does not require proving copyright infringement in model outputs.
insights.locator: On Friday, a judge largely denied a motion to dismiss

insights.claim: Reddit's unjust enrichment and unfair competition claims were tossed as preempted by the Copyright Act, narrowing the case to the DMCA anti-circumvention theory.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Preemption keeps state-law quasi-contract theories off the table for content platforms — DMCA circumvention is the remaining federal hook against scrapers.
insights.locator: This week wasn’t a total loss for SerpApi and Perplexity AI

insights.claim: Less than two weeks earlier a different court dismissed Google's similar action after finding Google had not proven that rights holders such as Reddit ever authorized the search engine to prevent scraping of protected content; Google said it plans to amend its complaint.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: The split outcome shows plaintiffs win or lose these cases on pleading specificity about licensing authorization, not on the underlying scraping conduct.
insights.locator: Engelmayer’s decision came less than two weeks after

themes.theme: The three-prong DMCA test as the operative framework

insights.claim: The operative legal test in these anti-scraping suits has three prongs: that defendants accessed snippets of works covered by the Copyright Act, that those works were protected by a technological measure effectively controlling access, and that defendants circumvented that technology.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Use this three-prong structure to handicap every pending scraper suit — the first prong is where cases have been dying.
insights.locator: For both Google and Reddit, the mission is to first prove

insights.claim: Google failed on the first prong while Reddit survived it because Reddit went beyond the bare allegation that it generally has licenses to display copyrighted content and instead pointed to specific licensing terms restricting use of its data.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Content owners with granular, enforceable licensing terms have a materially better litigation position than platforms relying on generic license language.
insights.locator: Google failed on the first prong

insights.claim: Engelmayer held that licensing deals need not be renegotiated every time a partner deploys new security technology, so Google SearchGuard can count as an authorized protection measure even though it was invented more than a year after the Google-Reddit licensing deal was struck.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: This retroactive-coverage reading is the most consequential holding for scrapers: existing licensing deals can silently acquire new anti-circumvention teeth as platforms ship new defenses.

themes.theme: Deletion promises as Reddit's legal hook

insights.claim: Reddit's surviving argument rests on a licensing term requiring partners like Google to delete posts Reddit flags when users remove content — millions of posts monthly — which unsanctioned scraping makes impossible to honor.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: User-deletion guarantees, not copyright ownership, are becoming the enforceable contractual asset platforms use against AI scraping — a template other UGC platforms can copy into their licensing terms.
insights.locator: Specifically, Reddit argued that when it licenses content to partners

insights.claim: Reddit successfully argued that letting deleted posts persist in Perplexity AI's answer engine harms both its reputation and its profits.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Framing scraping harm as a broken promise to users rather than lost licensing revenue is what got past the motion to dismiss — expect it to be copied.
insights.locator: And allowing deleted posts to fester in Perplexity AI’s answer engine

insights.claim: If Reddit wins, it would be positioned to force all AI scrapers into licensing agreements rather than negotiating them one at a time.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: A Reddit win converts scraped data into a paid input across the AI answer-engine sector, raising the cost base for retrieval-heavy AI products.
insights.locator: Reddit cheers; SerpApi prepares to fight

insights.claim: Reddit is seeking three injunctions: blocking SerpApi and Perplexity AI from accessing both Reddit and Google websites, stopping circumvention of Google SearchGuard, and barring use of previously scraped data.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: The demand to bar use of already-scraped data is the existential piece for a scraper-dependent answer engine, since it reaches back into deployed systems.
insights.locator: Reddit has asked the court for an injunction

insights.claim: SerpApi's defense is that it accesses public search results rather than Reddit's platform, and that public information does not become protected merely because a platform wants to charge for it.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: If this framing holds, the whole DMCA route against intermediaries collapses and licensing leverage reverts to whoever controls the search index.
insights.quote: SerpApi accesses public search results, not Reddit’s platform, and public information does not become protected because a platform wants to charge for it.
insights.locator: Asked for comment, Jeff Homrig, a lawyer for SerpApi

insights.claim: SerpApi frames both Google and Reddit as using the DMCA to wall off the open Internet by retroactively claiming control over content they neither authored nor own.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: This is the public-interest counter-narrative that will shape any appellate or legislative response to platform anti-scraping claims.
insights.quote: use the DMCA to wall off the open Internet by retroactively claiming control over content that they didn’t author and don’t own
insights.locator: Google told Ars that it planned to amend its complaint

insights.claim: Engelmayer noted SerpApi and Perplexity AI may still prove through discovery that Reddit never authorized Google to protect its content in search results, and a footnote suggested SerpApi could argue that all publicly accessible content in Google search results is not protected by the Copyright Act.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Surviving dismissal is a low bar here; the substantive questions on authorization and copyrightability are all still open going into discovery.
insights.locator: The fight is seemingly far from over

insights.claim: DMCA expert Meredith Rose of Public Knowledge argues Reddit is oddly positioned because DMCA standing normally requires being the copyright owner, the exclusive licensee, or the party deploying the technological protection measure — and Reddit is none of those things.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: The standing objection is the cleanest path to reversal on appeal, which caps how much a motion-to-dismiss win should move expectations.
insights.quote: Reddit is none of those things.

insights.claim: Rose characterizes Google and Reddit as grasping at whatever legal tool is available in the face of three years of rising AI scraping, and says DMCA rulings are driven more by vibes than doctrine, making winners hard to predict.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: High doctrinal variance means outcomes will be forum- and judge-dependent for years, favoring parties that can afford parallel suits.
insights.quote: sort of grasping at whatever tool is available
